options.text: The coordinate time measured in a frame where the events occur at different places
options.misconception: confuses coordinate time with invariant proper time

options.text: The proper time recorded by a clock present at both events in its rest frame

options.misconception: treats a moving observer's longer time as the minimum

options.misconception: uses light travel time instead of the spacetime interval

questions.explanation: Proper time is measured by a clock present at both events, so the events share one place in that frame, and it is the shortest interval between them. Any other inertial frame records a longer coordinate time.

questions.explanation: The contracted length is L0 over gamma, and at 0.80c gamma is 5/3, giving 120 times 3/5 equals 72 m. Length contracts only along the motion direction.

options.text: That simultaneity is relative and depends on the observer's frame
That light speed is different for moving and stationary observers
options.misconception: claims light speed varies
